current_bottleneck: 289d showed that simply adding latent token-state capacity is the wrong fix: it improved aggregate cointegration but destroyed the common cross-cell structure and level realism that 289c had recovered. The next bottleneck is preserving persistent history context during rollout without fragmenting the shared state.
last_result_summary: Iteration 122 ran 289d-v0 and regressed the world-model Stage A line from 3/11 to 2/11. The token-state branch improved aggregate cointegration to 1.192, but corr_ratio collapsed to 0.212 and the teacher-forced path itself became too smooth. The naive token-state capacity increase is therefore treated as falsified.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 289e-v0: return to the stronger 289c-style global latent state, but add explicit read-only history-memory access during rollout so the recurrent state can preserve longer-horizon context without a retrieval bank.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
